raw_text:
Here’s a structured 12-week muscle gain program tailored for a 26-year-old recreational lifter, strict vegan, with access to a full gym. The plan uses a phased progression, 4 days/week lifting, optional 1–2 short conditioning sessions, and a plant-only nutrition strategy targeting 150 g protein/day. 

Overview
- Goal: Hypertrophy with progressive overload, build foundational strength, improve movement quality, and support recovery.
- Split: Upper/Lower (4 days/week). Optional GPP/conditioning 1–2x/week (low-intensity).
- Phases:
  - Weeks 1–4: Foundation Hypertrophy + Technique (8–12 reps)
  - Weeks 5–8: Progressive Overload Hypertrophy (6–12 reps; intensity up)
  - Weeks 9–12: Intensification + Specialization (6–10 reps; added advanced techniques)
- Progression: Double progression (reps then load), RIR/RPE guided.
- Recovery: 1–2 rest days/week, deload built into Week 9 day-1 and day-2 volume reduction; monitor sleep and volume tolerance.
- Conditioning: Optional Zone 2 cardio 20–25 min 1–2x/week or 6–8k daily steps.

Key Training Guidelines
- Warm-up each session: 5–8 min light cardio, mobility for target joints, 2–3 ramp-up sets for first lift.
- Effort: Work sets mostly 1–3 RIR (RPE 7–9). Push close to failure on last set of accessories.
- Progression: When you hit top of rep range for all sets with given load, add 2–5% load next time. If you miss targets, keep load and aim to add reps next week.
- Tempo: Controlled eccentrics (2–3 sec) and strong concentric drive; 0–1 sec pause at the bottom on compound lifts as needed to maintain tension.
- Rest: Compounds 90–150 sec; accessories 60–90 sec; heavy lifts up to 2–3 min if needed.

Weekly Structure (example)
- Mon: Upper A
- Tue: Lower A
- Thu: Upper B
- Fri: Lower B
- Optional: Wed/Sat light cardio or mobility; Sun rest

Phase 1: Foundation Hypertrophy and Technique (Weeks 1–4)
Focus: Movement quality, establish volume baseline, 8–12 reps, 2–3 RIR.

Week 1–2
Upper A
- Bench press (barbell or DB): 3x8–10
- One-arm DB row: 3x10–12/side
- Seated DB shoulder press: 3x8–10
- Lat pulldown (medium-neutral): 3x10–12
- Incline DB bench: 2x10–12
- Cable lateral raise: 3x12–15
- Cable triceps pressdown (rope): 3x10–12
- EZ-bar curl or cable curl: 3x10–12

Lower A
- Back squat (high-bar): 3x8–10
- Romanian deadlift: 3x8–10
- Walking lunges: 2x10–12/leg
- Leg press (feet mid-stance): 3x10–12
- Seated leg curl: 3x10–12
- Standing calf raise: 3x12–15
- Cable woodchop or anti-rotation press: 2x12–15/side

Upper B
- Incline bench press (barbell or DB): 3x8–10
- Chest-supported T-bar row or machine row: 3x10–12
- Arnold press: 3x10–12
- Pull-ups or assisted pull-ups: 3x6–10
- Pec deck or cable fly: 2x12–15
- Rear delt cable fly: 3x12–15
- Overhead cable triceps extension: 3x10–12
- Incline DB curl: 3x10–12

Lower B
- Deadlift (conventional or trap bar): 3x5–6 (technique-focused; stop 2–3 RIR)
- Front squat or hack squat: 3x8–10
- Bulgarian split squat: 2x10–12/leg
- Hip thrust (barbell): 3x8–10
- Leg extension: 2x12–15
- Seated calf raise: 3x12–15
- Plank variations: 2x45–60 sec

Week 3–4
- Keep exercises; add 1 set to major compounds for priority areas if recovery is good:
  - Bench, squat, RDL, incline press, rows, hip thrust: move to 4 working sets.
  - Accessories stay 2–3 sets.
- Intensity: Edge closer to 1–2 RIR on last set of main lifts.
- Optional final set techniques on accessories: last set myo-reps or drop set on lateral raises or curls (keep form strict).

Phase 2: Progressive Overload Hypertrophy (Weeks 5–8)
Focus: Slightly heavier loads, 6–12 reps, modest volume bump, prioritize weak points.

Week 5–6
Upper A
- Bench press: 4x6–8
- One-arm DB row: 4x8–10/side
- Seated DB shoulder press: 3x8–10
- Weighted pull-ups or pulldown: 3x8–10
- Incline DB fly or cable fly: 2x12–15
- Lateral raise (cable or DB): 3x12–15
- Skull crusher or cable pressdown: 3x10–12
- Alternating DB curl: 3x10–12

Lower A
- Back squat: 4x6–8
- RDL: 4x6–8
- Leg press: 3x10–12
- Walking lunge: 3x10–12/leg
- Seated leg curl: 3x10–12
- Standing calf raise: 4x8–12
- Hanging knee raise: 3x10–15

Upper B
- Incline bench press: 4x6–8
- Machine row or chest-supported row: 4x8–10
- DB overhead press (slight incline or neutral): 3x8–10
- Wide-grip pulldown or pull-ups: 3x8–10
- Rear delt machine or cable reverse fly: 3x12–15
- Close-grip push-ups or dips (assisted): 2xAMRAP shy of failure
- EZ-bar curl: 3x8–10
- Cable hammer curl (rope): 2x10–12

Lower B
- Deadlift (conventional/trap): 4x4–6 (leave 1–2 RIR)
- Front squat or hack squat: 3x6–8
- Hip thrust: 4x8–10
- Bulgarian split squat: 3x8–10/leg
- Leg extension: 2x12–15
- Seated calf raise: 4x10–12
- Cable or machine crunch: 3x12–15

Week 7–8
- Keep structure, push loads 2–5% where reps at top end are achieved.
- Add one specialization “pump” set at the end for lagging muscle groups (e.g., delts, glutes, back): 1x15–20 with short rest, strict form.
- Maintain 1–2 cardio sessions but keep easy; avoid interfering with leg days.

Phase 3: Intensification + Specialization (Weeks 9–12)
Focus: Slightly heavier top sets, back-off volume, strategic intensifiers for hypertrophy without excessive fatigue. 6–10 reps main lifts, 8–15 accessories.

Week 9
- Slight deload on first two sessions: reduce volume by ~25–30% (drop one set from compounds, keep loads moderate).
Upper A
- Bench press: 1 top set 6–7 RPE x6–8, then 2x8–10 back-off at -10% load
- One-arm DB row: 3x8–10/side
- Seated DB press: 3x8–10
- Lat pulldown: 3x10–12
- Lateral raise: 3x12–15
- Triceps pressdown: 2x10–12
- Curl variation: 2x10–12

Lower A
- Back squat: 1 top set x6 at ~RPE 7–8, then 2x6–8 back-off
- RDL: 3x6–8
- Leg press: 2x10–12
- Leg curl: 2x10–12
- Calf raise: 3x10–12
- Core: 2 sets

Upper B
- Incline press: 1 top set x6–8, 2x8–10 back-off
- Row (machine/plate-loaded): 3x8–10
- Pull-ups or pulldown: 3x8–10
- Rear delt: 3x12–15
- Arms superset: Pressdown + curls 2x10–12 each

Lower B
- Deadlift: 3x3–5 at RPE 7–8 (perfect form), no grinders
- Front squat/hack: 3x6–8
- Hip thrust: 3x8–10
- Split squat: 2x8–10/leg
- Calves: 3x10–12
- Core: 2 sets

Week 10–11
- Return to full volume with top-set + back-off approach for big lifts.
- Include 1–2 carefully placed intensifiers on isolation work only (e.g., last set drop set on lateral raises or leg extensions, or rest-pause on curls or pressdowns).
- Keep RIR mostly 1–2; avoid failure on compounds.

Upper A
- Bench press: 1 top set x5–6 (RPE 8), then 3x6–8 back-off
- One-arm DB row: 4x8–10/side
- Seated DB press: 3x8–10
- Lat pulldown or weighted pull-ups: 3x8–10
- Incline cable fly: 2x12–15
- Lateral raise: 3x12–20 (last set drop set optional)
- Triceps pressdown: 3x10–12
- Cable curl: 3x10–12

Lower A
- Back squat: 1 top set x5–6 (RPE 8), then 3x6–8 back-off
- RDL: 4x6–8
- Walking lunge: 3x10–12/leg
- Leg curl: 3x10–12
- Standing calf raise: 4x8–12
- Ab wheel: 3x8–12

Upper B
- Incline press: 1 top set x5–6, then 3x6–8 back-off
- Machine row or chest-supported row: 4x8–10
- Pull-ups/pulldown: 3x8–10
- Rear delt cable fly: 3x12–15
- Close-grip machine press or dips (assisted): 2–3x8–10
- Hammer curl: 3x8–10
- Overhead cable triceps ext.: 3x10–12

Lower B
- Deadlift: 4x3–5 at RPE 7–8
- Front squat/hack squat: 3x6–8
- Hip thrust: 4x8–10
- Bulgarian split squat: 3x8–10/leg
- Leg extension: 2–3x12–15 (last set drop set optional)
- Seated calf raise: 4x10–12
- Cable crunch: 3x12–15

Week 12 (Overreach then taper at end of week)
- Days 1–3: Keep structure from Week 11; push accessories to the top of rep ranges, keep compounds at RPE 8 (do not max). 
- Day 4: Reduce volume by 40–50% to begin recovery. 
- Optional: End of week perform AMRAP set on a machine accessory for fun/feedback (e.g., leg press 1xAMRAP at a load you did for 12–15 last week; stop 1 rep before true failure).

Optional Conditioning/Mobility
- 1–2 sessions/week: 20–25 min Zone 2 bike/elliptical after upper days, or separate days. 
- Daily: 5–10 min mobility flows for hips, T-spine, shoulders.

Vegan Nutrition Plan: 150 g Protein/Day (Plant-Only)
Calorie targets
- For lean mass gain: Start ~200–300 kcal above maintenance. If bodyweight is stable by week 2, increase by 100–150 kcal. Aim for ~0.25–0.5 kg/month gain.
- Macro starting point: 2.0–2.2 g/kg protein (~150 g), 20–30% fat, remainder carbs for training performance.

Protein distribution
- 4–5 feedings/day with 25–40 g protein each to optimize muscle protein synthesis.
- Prioritize complete or complementary sources and leucine (~2–3 g/meal). Combine legumes + grains or use soy or pea blends.

Daily sample meal framework (approx 2,300–2,600 kcal depending on needs; adjust portions)
1) Breakfast
- Soy yogurt (unsweetened) 300 g + granola 60 g + mixed berries 150 g
- Hemp seeds 1.5 tbsp
Approx: 35 g protein, 75 g carbs, 18 g fat

2) Mid-morning
- Protein shake: 1.5 scoops pea/rice blend (30–35 g protein) + banana
Approx: 32 g protein, 35–40 g carbs, 2–4 g fat

3) Lunch
- Tofu bowl: Extra-firm tofu 200–250 g (pan-seared) + quinoa 1 cup cooked + edamame 100 g + mixed veg + tahini lemon sauce (1 tbsp)
Approx: 45 g protein, 65–75 g carbs, 18–20 g fat

4) Pre-workout snack (60–90 min pre)
- Sourdough 2 slices + hummus 3–4 tbsp + cherry tomatoes
Approx: 18–20 g protein, 60–70 g carbs, 10–12 g fat

5) Post-workout/dinner
- Tempeh 200 g + brown rice 1 cup cooked + stir-fry veg + pineapple side
Approx: 40–45 g protein, 70–80 g carbs, 10–12 g fat

Notes and swaps
- Protein powders: Choose a blend (pea+rice) or soy isolate. Check for B12-fortified options or add separate B12.
- Protein staples per serving (approx):
  - Firm tofu 200 g: ~24–30 g
  - Tempeh 200 g: ~36–40 g
  - Seitan 150 g: ~30–35 g (gluten)
  - Edamame 100 g: ~11 g
  - Lentils 1 cup cooked: ~18 g
  - Chickpeas 1 cup cooked: ~14 g
  - Soy yogurt 300 g: ~18–24 g
  - Pea/rice/soy isolate: 25–30 g/scoop
- Complementary combos: Lentils + rice; hummus + whole grain pita; peanut butter + soy milk smoothie with powder; bean chili + corn tortillas.
- Pre/post timing: 
  - Pre: 30–90 min before lifting, 30–60 g easily digested carbs + 20–30 g protein.
  - Post: Within 1–2 hours, target 30–45 g protein + 60–90 g carbs.
- Hydration: 30–40 ml/kg/day water baseline; add 500–1000 ml around training. Consider 1/8–1/4 tsp salt in preworkout drink on hot/sweaty days.
- Creatine: 3–5 g/day (vegan-friendly monohydrate). Take daily anytime.
- Omega-3: Algae-based DHA/EPA 300–600 mg/day.
- B12: 1,000 mcg cyanocobalamin 2–3x/week or 50–100 mcg daily.
- Iron/Zinc: Monitor ferritin; include legumes, tofu, pumpkin seeds; use vitamin C with iron-rich meals; separate coffee/tea from iron meals.
- Calcium/Vitamin D: Fortified plant milks/yogurts; 1,000–1,200 mg Ca/day; Vitamin D3 (vegan) 1,000–2,000 IU/day depending on sun.

Example 7-day protein plan (all plant-only; mix and match)
- Day A: 2 shakes (30 g each), tofu lunch (30 g), tempeh dinner (35 g), soy yogurt + seeds (25 g) = ~150 g
- Day B: Seitan stir-fry (35 g), lentil pasta bowl (25 g), edamame snack (15 g), tofu scramble (30 g), shake (30 g), soy milk latte (5 g) = ~140–150 g
- Day C: Chickpea wrap + seitan slices (35 g), quinoa + black beans (25 g), shake (30 g), soy yogurt (20 g), roasted tofu (30 g) = ~140–150 g
Adjust portions to ensure 150 g hit daily.

Recovery and Lifestyle
- Sleep: 7.5–9 hours/night, consistent schedule.
- Stress: 5–10 min daily breathwork or mindfulness.
- Deload indicators: Persistent soreness, sleep disruption, plateau or drop in bar speed; if present, reduce sets by 30% for a week.
- Track: Bodyweight 3x/week (AM, average weekly), performance logs, progress photos every 4 weeks.
- Female-specific note: If menstrual cycle symptoms affect performance, place slightly lighter workouts during days 1–2 as needed and push hard days when energy is higher (often late follicular/ovulatory phase).

Progress Checkpoints
- Week 4: Review volume tolerance and weak points; adjust specialization sets.
- Week 8: Increase cals by 100–200 if scale hasn’t moved; ensure 150 g protein consistently.
- Week 12: Taper end of week, then test rep PRs the following week on key lifts at submax loads.

This template gives you clear week-by-week structure, exercise selection, progression, and a robust vegan nutrition plan to reliably hit 150 g protein/day while driving hypertrophy.
